walkthroughs.body_html: Arctic Amplification: the Arctic has warmed ~3.1degC since 1971, roughly four times the global average (NOAA Arctic Report Card 2022). Causes include the ice-albedo feedback: sea ice (albedo ~0.8) is replaced by dark ocean (albedo ~0.06), absorbing more solar energy. Summer sea ice extent has declined ~40% since 1979, with September 2012 reaching a record minimum of 3.4 million km2.

Northern Hemisphere permafrost stores ~1,500 PgC, twice atmospheric carbon. Thaw releases CO2 and the more potent CH4 (28x GWP over 100yr). The 2020 Verkhoyansk record of 38degC accelerated thaw; thermokarst lakes proliferate across Siberia. The 2020 Norilsk diesel spill (21,000 tonnes) was attributed to permafrost subsidence damaging tank foundations. Estimated emissions: 0.3-0.6 PgC/yr by 2100.

Several positive feedbacks operate: 1) ice-albedo loss accelerates warming; 2) permafrost thaw releases CO2/CH4; 3) boreal wildfires (record 2021 Yakutia) release stored carbon and reduce albedo via soot; 4) submarine clathrate destabilisation could release methane on continental shelves. The 2022 IPCC AR6 lists Arctic systems among high-risk tipping elements with potential to push global warming beyond 2degC even with mitigation.

mcqs.q: What is a positive climate feedback loop?
options: A process where warming triggers changes that cause more warming — e.g. melting Arctic ice exposes dark ocean, which absorbs more heat, melting more ice (ice-albedo feedback).
A tipping point is when world leaders agree to act on climate change.
Positive feedback means a good outcome for the climate.
Positive feedback means the climate balances itself out.

mcqs.q: What causes global sea level rise?
options: Sea level rises mainly because Arctic sea ice is melting.
Two main factors: thermal expansion of warming seawater, and the melting of land-based ice (glaciers and ice sheets) adding water to oceans.
Positive feedback means the climate balances itself out.
Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.

mcqs.q: What is a climate tipping point?
options: A threshold beyond which a system changes irreversibly into a new state — e.g. the Amazon flipping from rainforest to savanna, or Greenland's ice sheet committing to total melt.
A tipping point is when world leaders agree to act on climate change.
A tipping point is just when warming reaches 1.5 degrees C.
Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.
